record.original_question: For a numerical semigroup Gamma = <g1 < g2 < ... < ge>, define its width by width(Gamma) = ge - g1. For each positive integer w, let W(w) be the supremum of rho(Gamma) over all numerical semigroups Gamma with width(Gamma) = w, where rho(Gamma) is the number of relations in a minimal presentation of Gamma. Determine W(w).

evidence.quote: The width of a numerical semigroup Γ = hg1 < g2 < ··· < gei is defined as width(Γ ) = ge −g1. ... Problem 7. Let w ∈ N. Determine W (w) := sup{ ρ(Γ ) | width(Γ ) = w }.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a cofinite subset $\Gamma \subseteq \mathbb{N} = \{0,1,2,\dots\}$ that contains $0$ and is closed under addition. Every numerical semigroup admits a unique minimal system of generators $g_1 < g_2 < \cdots < g_e$ with $\gcd(g_1,\dots,g_e)=1$, and we write $\Gamma = \langle g_1,\dots,g_e\rangle$. The width of $\Gamma$ is defined by
$$\operatorname{width}(\Gamma) := g_e - g_1.$$
Consider the surjective monoid homomorphism $\varphi : \mathbb{N}^e \to \Gamma$ sending the $i$-th standard basis vector to $g_i$. The kernel congruence $\ker\varphi = \{(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b}) \in \mathbb{N}^e \times \mathbb{N}^e : \varphi(\mathbf{a}) = \varphi(\mathbf{b})\}$ admits a minimal generating set (a minimal presentation) as a congruence, and all such minimal presentations have the same finite cardinality. Denote this cardinality by $\rho(\Gamma)$, the number of relations in a minimal presentation of $\Gamma$.

For each positive integer $w$, define
$$W(w) := \sup\{\rho(\Gamma) : \Gamma \text{ is a numerical semigroup with } \operatorname{width}(\Gamma) = w\}.$$

Determine $W(w)$ as a function of $w$ (in particular, decide whether it is finite, and if so give a closed-form expression or sharp bounds).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a recent compilation of open problems on relations of numerical semigroups. The general behavior of $\rho(\Gamma)$ even under fixed invariants (such as embedding dimension or width) remains poorly understood, and no closed-form expression for $W(w)$ appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on relations of numerical semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work collects open problems about minimal presentations of numerical semigroups, including questions about the maximal number of relations under width constraints.
status_evidence.claim: The determination of W(w) is listed among open problems concerning minimal presentations.

status_evidence.title: On minimal presentations of numerical monoids
status_evidence.snippet: The question of how many relations a numerical monoid can have is still not well understood despite the simplicity of the objects involved.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp bounds on the number of minimal relations of numerical semigroups remain an active and unresolved area of research.
